params.body:
The pipeline on Gentells Standard 0.8.0 (Trendwolves/gentells-standard#12, tag `v0.8.0`): Trendwolves' own birth years and lifestage ages, and the tagging rules in `rules/cohort.json`.

## What changes

- **Sync:** `bin/sync-standard.mjs` pins `v0.8.0`, and `packages/core/standard.mjs` and the conformance fixture are regenerated.
- **Rules ported to `standard-rules.mjs`:**
  - `cohortOf` leaves out the lenses (ZAlpha, Tweens).
  - New: `lensesOf`, `generationsOf`, `lifestageBorn`, `lifestagesOf`, `generationOfLifestage`, `lifestageLabel`.
  - The standard's new conformance cases run against the port in `test/standard.test.mjs`.
- **Classifier: ages in, birth years worked out in code** (`packages/core/cohort-tags.mjs`).
  - The model reports the ages it reads (`ages: {from, to}`).
  - The generations and the lifestages under 18 are worked out from those ages at the signal's own year: `published_at`, else `ingested_at`.
  - A micro generation (ZAlpha) is set only when it holds more than half of the birth years.
  - The model still sets a generation the text names without an age, and the lifestages that status decides from 18.
  - Each signal line in the prompt now carries `date=`.
  - Before, the model did this arithmetic itself with the current year, so a signal from 2025 was read a year off.
- **One set of cohort instructions:** `cohortInstructions` in `classify-prompt.mjs` is shared by `classify.mjs` and `retag-cohort.mjs`, so a re-tag asks exactly what the classifier asks. It covers the 0.8.0 rules: Teens from 11 (own smartphone), Tweens also Kids, nothing under 6, status decides from 18, never Gen Beta.
- **`splitCohorts`:**
  - drops a reserved generation (Gen Beta);
  - adds Kids to every Tweens tag.
- **Labels:** a lifestage label carries its range, "Teens (11–17)", through `LIFESTAGE_LABEL` and the projection, so the site shows it without a change of its own. Young Families is no longer marked proposed.
- **`derive-cohort.mjs`:** a trend also carries a lens when more than half its tagged signals do.
- **`retag-cohort.mjs`:**
  - uses the shared instructions and each signal's own year;
  - writes the standard version into its dry run;
  - `--apply` refuses a file made under another version, so the 0.7.0 dry runs on the box cannot be applied by mistake.
- **`bin/posts-to-json.py`:** the keyword ages now follow 0.8.0 (nine and ten are Tweens; eleven and twelve are Teens).

## What does not change on deploy

No stored tag moves on deploy:
- The start-up cohort migrations ran once in September and stay done.
- Bringing stored tags in line (Tweens rows gain Kids) is the manual `bin/standard-migrate.mjs`: plan first, then `--apply` with an undo per version.
- The re-tag stays a dry run until its numbers are reviewed.

## Tests

`node --test test/*.test.mjs`: 1031 pass. Six report-render tests fail locally only, because `pdftoppm` is missing on this machine; CI installs it. The tests that pinned 0.7.0 values (ZAlpha 2008–2013, Young Families proposed, labels without a range, Tweens without Kids) now pin 0.8.0, and `test/cohort-tags.test.mjs` is new.

## Next

1. A dry run of `retag-cohort.mjs` under 0.8.0, for review before anything is written.
2. `bin/standard-migrate.mjs` (plan first).
3. Site: the fallback taxonomy, the Young Families filter test, and the MCP description.
params.title: Gentells Standard 0.8.0: ages read at the signal's year, generations from birth years
